Delinquent

dih-LING-kwunt -- Latin delinquere, 'to fail in duty, leave undone': one who leaves duty behind. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Delinquent is tending to commit crimes or neglect duties.

Counselors at the center work to steer delinquent teens toward school and steady jobs.

Worked Example

Instead of going to class, a group of teenagers spends the semester spray-painting rail cars, shoplifting snacks, and daring each other to break into the empty pool after dark.

That pattern of lawbreaking and dodged responsibility is exactly what delinquent describes. Unlike 'mischievous,' which suggests playful trouble, delinquent behavior crosses into genuine rule-breaking and crime.

How Delinquent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

wayward

wayward: stubbornly straying from what is right

lawless

lawless: ignoring or defying the law entirely

offending

offending: committing offenses or breaking rules

Antonyms

law-abiding

law-abiding: faithfully obeying the law

dutiful

dutiful: reliably meeting one's obligations

How Strong Is It? — wayward → lawless → delinquent

wayward vs. delinquent

wayward vs. delinquent: Wayward is softer than delinquent -- a wayward teen strays from the expected path, while a delinquent one has crossed into actual rule-breaking or crime.

lawless vs. delinquent

lawless vs. delinquent: Lawless is broader and harsher than delinquent: delinquent usually describes young people drifting into crime, while lawless can describe hardened criminals or entire places where law has collapsed.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — de-

prefix — de-: away, completely (Latin)

root — -linqu-

root — -linqu-: to leave (Latin (linquere))

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: adjective-forming: in a state of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin delinquere meant 'to fail in duty' -- literally to leave one's obligations behind -- from de- ('away') and linquere ('to leave'), the same root that gives us relinquish and this unit's derelict.

Use the root in a new word: relinquish

Use the root in a new word: relinquish: The champion refused to relinquish her title without one final match.

Root Check

Word Choice

Delinquent most often describes young people in trouble with the law -- 'juvenile delinquent' is a set phrase -- and in financial contexts it describes overdue obligations, as in 'a delinquent account.'
